replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical procedure that uses an orthogonal transformation to convert a set of observations of possibly correlated variables into a set of values of linearly uncorrelated variables called principal components. To perform PCA, you first need to standardize your data. Then, you compute the covariance matrix. Next, you compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. Finally, you sort the eigenvalues in descending order and choose the top k eigenvalues. The corresponding eigenvectors form the principal components.
